source.title: Large Batch Optimization for Deep Learning: Training BERT in 76 minutes
source.authors: Yang You; Jing Li; Sashank J. Reddi; Jonathan Hseu; Sanjiv Kumar; Srinadh Bhojanapalli; Xiao-Dan Song; J. Demmel; K. Keutzer; Cho-Jui Hsieh

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares optimizer and batch-size choices using held-out validation or dev performance, a conceptual test of V4 and V5. It does not measure the training-to-test error gap directly.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper's own optimizer comparisons and batch-size sweeps. Cited findings from other studies are not included. The BERT dev set is called test data in the paper; results are F1 scores, not error rates.
record.test_reason: Fixed-epoch batch sweeps measure held-out performance relevant to V5. Image-classification optimizer comparisons bear on V4. Neither version requires an explicit training-to-test gap measurement. The study is not an original source for either version.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly accurate. Specify that the 76-minute BERT run uses 64K batches during short-sequence pretraining and 32K during long-sequence pretraining, with renewed warmup. Its downstream F1 retains the published baseline but is below small-batch LAMB. The authors also conclude that existing adaptive solvers perform poorly on ImageNet or are difficult to tune, while LAMB reaches competitive ResNet-50 accuracy.
record.recipe_differences: Uses LAMB, an adaptive elementwise and layerwise optimizer, with square-root learning-rate scaling and warmup. The paper compares held-out performance across optimizers and batch sizes; it does not reproduce the original studies' methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Held-out scores vary with optimizer and batch size. BERT mixed-batch training uses a second-stage learning-rate re-warmup; ResNet-50 results report square-root learning-rate scaling and warmup across batch sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: LAMB outperforms LARS at each reported BERT batch size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Elementwise plus layerwise adaptation outperforms layerwise momentum adaptation on downstream BERT SQuAD performance.

record.problems: The study reports validation accuracy and dev F1 rather than training-to-test error gaps. The BERT dev-set scores follow SQuAD fine-tuning and should not be treated as direct pretraining generalization measures. Some table formatting is flattened, and uncertainty estimates are not reported.
record.rows_left_out: No required results omitted. Other appendix optimizer sweeps and small-dataset comparisons were not extracted because they are outside the tested claim-version comparisons or duplicate the optimizer evidence summarized above.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and chance-level held-out performance under random labels.
Width beyond interpolation and its effect on test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Switching Adam to SGD, word-level language modeling, and equal or better training performance accompanying worse held-out performance. BERT comparisons do not include an ordinary SGD control.

Longer-training recovery, isolated causal effects of warmup or learning-rate scaling, and systematic normalization or regularization interventions. BERT outcomes measure downstream SQuAD performance rather than held-out pretraining loss.
Dropout interventions and removal of dropout with weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and correlations with generalization gaps.

missing.what: Reconstruct LARS's fixed-epoch batch sweep as V5 rows: F1 is 90.717 at 512, 89.589 at 16K, and training diverges at 32K. Existing rows encode cross-optimizer comparisons instead.

Restore the declared small-dataset exclusions because they directly bear on V4: Table 6's CIFAR-10 optimizer comparison and Table 7's MNIST five-run means. Their contrasting optimizer rankings matter for scope.

record.verdict_notes: All judgments use the supplied text. Momentum's ImageNet comparison is a cited reference, and score differences generally lack uncertainty estimates. Optimizer and batch comparisons should not be interpreted as isolating generalization from optimization failure. The small-dataset results were declared omitted, but their stated exclusion as outside the claim comparisons is incorrect.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization are not measured.
No width sweep or interpolation-threshold test.
No convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison.

The paper tests LAMB, Adam, AdaGrad, AdamW, LARS and momentum comparisons on BERT and ImageNet/ResNet-50, plus small-data optimizer comparisons. It does not test switching from Adam to SGD or language-model word-level outcomes.

Batch-size sweeps use LAMB on BERT and ImageNet/ResNet-50 with fixed epochs; the mixed-batch BERT run changes the batch by stage and re-warms up. It does not test language models beyond BERT or systematically vary normalization and regularization.
No magnitude-aware sharpness or generalization-measure comparison.
